fixed_ritz_standard_sw_every_fixed_order.exact_assumptions: At fixed M on a finite connected zero-source Q3 spatial graph with deg(x)>=1, each onsite Ritz space is finite dimensional; H0=sum_x k_(x,M)>=0, P0=tensor_x P_x is the tensor product of onsite ground projectors, and every onsite excitation gap is at least Gamma. Choose omega_(x,e)>=0 on incident edges with sum_(e containing x) omega_(x,e)=1; on the periodic coordination-z graph use omega_(x,e)=1/z. For e={x,y}, define tilde B_(e,M)=B_(e,M)+delta_1[omega_(x,e)P_(1,x)+omega_(y,e)P_(1,y)], V_M=sum_e tilde B_(e,M), H_M(lambda)=sum_x k_(x,M)+lambda V_M, and J_M=max_x sum_(e containing x)||tilde B_(e,M)||. The onsite allocation identity sum_e delta_1[omega_(x,e)P_(1,x)+omega_(y,e)P_(1,y)]=delta_1 sum_x P_(1,x) makes H_M(1) exactly the physical zero-source fixed-M Q3 Hamiltonian up to the removed scalar. The onsite ground projector may have arbitrary finite rank, hence the Q3 rank-two P_x is allowed. The subtraction k=h_site-epsilon_0-delta_1 P_1 makes phi_0 and phi_1 exact zero modes of H0, while the allocated term restores their physical splitting at lambda=1. Constants may depend on M, J_M, ||k_M||/Gamma and degree.
fixed_ritz_standard_sw_every_fixed_order.linked_theorem: For every fixed n, the multivariate standard-SW coefficient H_eff,n=sum_C K_(n,C) has K_(n,C)=0 unless C is connected and |C|<=n, and K_(n,C) acts only on the vertex support Lambda(C). This fixed-coefficient theorem needs no convergence of the full SW series.
fixed_ritz_standard_sw_every_fixed_order.count: A safe rooted ordered connected n-edge tuple count is (n!)^2 z^n: choose one of n! edge-growth orders, then at step j use at most jz incidences. Thus support is at most n+1 and diameter at most n. The count is deliberately nonoptimal.
fixed_ritz_standard_sw_every_fixed_order.boundary: Fixed finite M and fixed n only. The theorem does not provide an M-uniform coefficient norm, n-to-infinity convergence, an all-order QPS sum, or physical lambda=1 control.

fixed_ritz_each_fixed_order_small_coupli.primary_source: Bravyi-DiVincenzo-Loss 2011, Theorems 1, 3 and 4 and the Section 4 normalization above.
fixed_ritz_each_fixed_order_small_coupli.scaled_coupling: For H_M(lambda)=sum_x k_(x,M)+lambda V_M with V_M=sum_e tilde B_(e,M) and J_M=max_x sum_(e containing x)||tilde B_(e,M)||, write eta=lambda J_M after normalizing the augmented fixed-M interaction to local strength one. The physical zero-source fixed-M Q3 Hamiltonian is H_M(1), where eta=J_M. For each fixed truncation order n there are positive epsilon_(c,n,M) and C_(n,M), independent of |Lambda|, such that |eta|<epsilon_(c,n,M) gives |E_0(H_M(lambda))-E_0(H_SW,std^[n](lambda))| and |E_0(H_M(lambda))-E_0(H_SW,loc^[n](lambda))| at most C_(n,M)|Lambda||eta|^(n+1). The standard/local truncations are related inside P0 by a low-space unitary up to the same extensive order.
fixed_ritz_each_fixed_order_small_coupli.dependence: The threshold and constant may depend on n, M, J_M, ||k_M||/Gamma and graph degree. In the local-SW proof the displayed fixed-order scale degrades as Omega(Gamma n^-2) after unit-strength normalization.
fixed_ritz_each_fixed_order_small_coupli.convergence_boundary: The global standard-SW analytic radius obtained from the total operator norm scales at best as Gamma/(16||V_M||), hence generally as 1/|Lambda|; the local all-order radius quoted in the paper is also volume shrinking. The fixed-order extensive theorem is therefore not an all-order volume-uniform convergence theorem.
fixed_ritz_each_fixed_order_small_coupli.scope: No claim is made at physical lambda=1 unless its scaled coupling separately satisfies the fixed-(n,M) hypothesis; no uniformity in M or limit n to infinity is asserted.

zero_source_q3_third_fourth_order_coeffi.local_block_hypotheses: At zero source let B_f be the bare nonnegative Q3 edge interaction and tilde B_f its onsite-allocated physical edge. Relative to the rank-two local projector P_f set A_f=P_f B_f P_f, tilde A_f=P_f tilde B_f P_f, L_f=Q_f B_f P_f=Q_f tilde B_f P_f, U_f=Q_f B_f Q_f, and tilde U_f=Q_f tilde B_f Q_f. Define k_f:=k_x+k_y. Use ||A_f||<=a, ||L_f||<=epsilon and 0<=U_f<=rho_b k_f as quadratic forms. The onsite projections obey P_(1,x)P_(1,y)<=P_f; hence on Q_f the eigenvalue-two branch of P_(1,x)+P_(1,y) is removed and 0<=Q_f[P_(1,x)+P_(1,y)]Q_f<=Q_f<=k_f/Gamma, while ||P_f[P_(1,x)+P_(1,y)]P_f||=2. The allocated onsite term is diagonal in the local P_f/Q_f decomposition, so it adds no cross leg. For periodic omega=1/z, ||tilde A_f||<=a_tilde:=a+2delta_1/z and 0<=tilde U_f<=rho_tilde k_f with rho_tilde:=rho_b+delta_1/(z Gamma). For the registered inputs delta_1=1/10000, z=6 and Gamma=100, a_tilde=32063/500000 and rho_tilde=2918597/30000000. In the global Q decomposition the augmented local-high and outside-high locally-low diagonal sectors are orthogonal, so their sandwiched contribution is max(rho_tilde,a_tilde/Gamma); here rho_tilde>=a_tilde/Gamma. Adding the unchanged two cross legs gives ||W_f||<=w_tilde for W_f=R^(1/2)Q tilde B_f Q R^(1/2), w_tilde=max(rho_tilde,a_tilde/Gamma)+2epsilon/Gamma=584161/6000000.
zero_source_q3_third_fourth_order_coeffi.coefficient_bounds: Let T_e=Q tilde B_e P and E_e=R^(1/2)T_e. Then ||E_e||<=epsilon/sqrt(Gamma). Every connected ordered third-order coefficient is at most per3=epsilon^2(w_tilde/Gamma+a_tilde/Gamma^2). Every connected ordered fourth-order sequential coefficient is at most per4=epsilon^4/Gamma^3+(epsilon^2/Gamma)(w_tilde+a_tilde/Gamma)^2.
zero_source_q3_third_fourth_order_coeffi.qps_bounds: For disjoint components X,Y, the direct formula Theta4_seq=(1/2){F,B}-S*RS is additive. B and F split into single-component pieces. Its cross-double term is S_XY=-(T_X tensor D_Y+D_X tensor T_Y)=-(K_X+K_Y)(D_X tensor D_Y), hence R_XY S_XY=-D_X tensor D_Y and S_XY* R_XY S_XY=B_X tensor F_Y+F_X tensor B_Y. These are exactly the mixed terms in (1/2){F,B}, so every disconnected multivariate fourth-order edge coefficient vanishes; orthogonal single-excitation sectors leave Theta4_X tensor P_Y+P_X tensor Theta4_Y. Therefore the safe connected rooted count applies. Retaining the v2.5 safe third-order count gives ||Theta3||_aQPS<=48z(2z-1)^2 exp(3aQPS) per3. The safe fourth-order count is 5(4!)^2 z^4=2880 z^4, so ||Theta4||_aQPS<=2880 z^4 exp(4aQPS) per4. Both constants are independent of spatial volume and Ritz cutoff for the declared zero-source Q3 block constants.
zero_source_q3_third_fourth_order_coeffi.ritz_removal: For nested parity-preserving onsite spectral Ritz projections Pi_M containing P and commuting with K, Pi_M tends strongly to one. Each local E_e is finite rank, hence Pi_M E_e tends to E_e in norm; the uniformly bounded compressions Pi_M W_f Pi_M converge strongly, and their action on the finite-rank ranges converges in norm. Every fixed connected third- and fourth-order coefficient therefore converges in operator norm, and the finite rooted cluster counts pass this convergence to the displayed QPS norms.
zero_source_q3_third_fourth_order_coeffi.boundary: This closes the actual unbounded zero-source Q3 coefficient construction and Ritz removal only at orders three and four. It supplies no fifth-order estimate, all-order recursion convergence, physical phase transfer or GNS gap.

fixed_finite_volume_and_ritz_complete_fo.setup: At fixed finite Lambda,M retain H=K+lambda(V_d+V_od), V_d=A direct-sum C, T=QVP, R=(QKQ)^(-1), D=RT, G=D-D*, S=RTA-CRT, Z=RS and G2=Z-Z*. A third generator may remove the order-three off-diagonal block but cannot change the order-four low block.
fixed_finite_volume_and_ritz_complete_fo.sequential_formula: With B=T*RT and F=T*R^2T, the complete sequential fourth-order low block is Theta4_seq=(1/8)P ad_G^3(V_od)P+(1/2)P[G2,[G,V_d]]P=(1/2){F,B}-S*RS. Equivalently Theta4_seq=(1/2){F,B}-S*RS.

fixed_finite_volume_and_ritz_complete_fo.linked_boundary: BDL Theorem 2 supplies connected support for the standard-gauge coefficient. Independently, the direct sequential formula is additive on disjoint components: its S_XY*R_XY S_XY term equals B_X tensor F_Y+F_X tensor B_Y and cancels the mixed part of (1/2){F,B}. Thus every disconnected multivariate fourth-order edge coefficient vanishes before applying the connected rooted count. The low-space gauge commutator gives the fixed-order crosswalk; no equality of sequential and standard coefficient matrices is claimed when A is non-scalar.
fixed_finite_volume_and_ritz_complete_fo.scope: Complete algebraic coefficient and gauge crosswalk at fixed finite Lambda,M; not a BCH convergence theorem or an all-order oscillator elimination.
